items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Dan LeBlanc read fairly well. He was the tuba player

ctx.x: and it's the 10th of November, 1986. Who were the leaders and managers of the Owls through the years?

Earl Crum was the manager. Leader? I don't think there was any leader. They just put the music out there on the stand and they went along and if they did any improvising they did it as a group to go along there, but they didn't read too well. You agree with me, Godfrey? Yeah. Sieg Christensen, when he joined the band, he read fairly well and Dan LeBlanc read fairly well. He was the tuba player and Bill read a little bit, trumpet player and Pinky didn't read that well, but Benji White, he carried the sax section.…
And then after Crum left, what happened? How did that happen? Well, after Crum left,

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: No, no. I was on some bone now. And Dan, when the orchestra broke up, Dan went to school.

ctx.x: Did you play any tuba with the owls ever? No. You didn't? No, no. Did you play string bass with the owls at the same time when Dan LeBlanc was around playing tuba?

No, no. I was on some bone now. And Dan, when the orchestra broke up, Dan went to school. He went to Loyola and became a teacher. Became a teacher? Yeah. He played too, he played too. What did he teach? Do you remember? He taught in St. Bernard Parish. He taught at school and the system there. Music? Yeah, he taught music. And I could never stand Lou Wap, why he didn't give him a job, with all of these funny yokels they had, you know, around there that he put on. And of course, Lou Wap, I don't want to say that.…
You played with Tony Amarico in that band. You played with him some other times too, didn't you?
